name: Issachar
overview: Issachar was the ninth-born son of Jacob and the fifth son of Leah, belonging to the tribe of Issachar. He was a male figure in the patriarchal lineage of Israel. The biblical record identifies him primarily through his birth order and tribal association.
namesAndTitles: The name Issachar means 'there is reward,' reflecting a meaning given in Genesis 30:18. This name does not appear to have been directly given by God but rather by his parents, conveying a sense of recompense or blessing associated with his birth.
familyAndRelationships: Issachar was a son of Jacob and Leah and had several brothers, including Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Zebulun, and Dinah, as well as half-brothers Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph, and Benjamin. He was also the father of Tola. These relationships place him firmly within the twelve tribes of Israel as one of the patriarchal sons.
scriptureSignificance: Issachar holds significance as the progenitor of the tribe that bore his name, noted for wisdom and discernment of times and seasons in Israel’s history. His birth followed the episode involving mandrakes, and his name symbolizes a divine reward, marking his role in God's unfolding plan through Jacob's descendants. The tribe of Issachar contributed to Israel’s understanding of God's timing and guidance.
